boards.title: Your First Weekend at James Madison University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence connecting JMU landmarks, student recreation, public science, green space, and downtown Harrisonburg without assuming a particular event calendar.

cards.title: Start Friday on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Historic Bluestone campus
cards.notes: Begin beneath Wilson Hall, walk the Bluestone paths, and use this open campus landmark to orient yourself before heading indoors.
cards.short_summary: Get your bearings in JMU’s historic campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU identifies the Quad as its oldest campus area, lined by Bluestone buildings, capped by Wilson Hall, and used as a gathering space for more than 110 years.
cards.access_notes: An outdoor campus landmark; follow posted campus restrictions and avoid disrupting scheduled activities.

cards.title: Meet Little Jimmy
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Between Varner House and Logan Hall
cards.notes: Find the life-size Madison statue near the Quad and take a quick group photo before continuing toward The Union.
cards.short_summary: Put a face—and a photo stop—to the university’s namesake.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU documents the campus statue nicknamed Little Jimmy as a favorite photo location and says its 5-foot-4-inch scale matches President James Madison’s height.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark near the Quad; view it from established campus walkways.

cards.title: Play a Round at The Union
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Warren Hall
cards.notes: Bring your JACard, find the student lounges, and use the free pool tables for an easy first-night activity with new classmates.
cards.short_summary: Turn Friday evening into a low-pressure game night.
cards.evidence_claim: The Union’s official page lists student lounges, a movie theater, and free pool tables among the building’s amenities.
cards.source_title: The Union at James Madison University - JMU
cards.access_notes: Use during posted building hours; some areas or after-hours entrances may require an active JACard.

cards.title: Browse the Saturday Market
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Turner Pavilion downtown
cards.notes: Walk the producer-only stalls, compare seasonal goods, and treat buying breakfast or crafts as optional rather than assumed.
cards.short_summary: Start Saturday among regional growers, makers, and prepared-food vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: The market’s official site identifies it as a producer-only market at 228 South Liberty Street and lists Saturday sessions year-round.
cards.access_notes: Saturday hours vary by season: the official site lists 8 a.m.–1 p.m. April–November and 9 a.m.–1 p.m. December–March.

cards.title: Circle Plecker Pond
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · University Boulevard
cards.notes: Enter from Lot R5 or the welcome center, follow the accessible pond loop, and leave plants, wildlife, and water features undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: Trade downtown pavement for an accessible garden-and-pond loop.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU states that the arboretum grounds are free to the public from dawn to dusk daily and describes Plecker Pond Loop as fully accessible.
cards.access_notes: Grounds are open dawn to dusk, 365 days a year; stay on appropriate paths and follow the posted preserve guidelines.

cards.title: Try the One-Mile Trail Loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · UREC-to-Arboretum trail system
cards.notes: Choose the marked one-mile loop, wear shoes for mixed surfaces, and skip longer sections if construction notices remain posted.
cards.short_summary: Add a short, clearly marked trail segment between campus destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU Recreation documents one-, two-, and three-mile trail loops connecting UREC, the arboretum, and University Park, with varied surfaces and steep terrain in places.
cards.access_notes: Check the official page for construction notices; trails include chipped wood, gravel, concrete, inclines, and declines.

cards.title: Catch a Saturday Sky Show
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Miller Hall
cards.notes: Check the current program, arrive before your chosen public show, and pair the full-dome movie with its accompanying star talk.
cards.short_summary: Spend Saturday afternoon under a full-dome simulated sky.
cards.evidence_claim: The planetarium’s official page says its Saturday public shows are free and lists family shows at 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. plus feature shows at 2:15 and 3:30 p.m.
cards.source_title: Welcome to the John C. Wells Planetarium - JMU
cards.access_notes: Verify the current calendar before going; closures, university breaks, delays, or special programming can affect shows.

cards.title: Learn Your Way Around UREC
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon · Driver Drive
cards.notes: Swipe in with your JACard, tour the main activity areas, and choose a familiar first activity rather than committing to a full workout.
cards.short_summary: Make the large recreation center feel manageable on your first visit.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU’s UREC guide says students have a membership, enter with a JACard or the UREC app, and can use programs spanning aquatics, fitness, intramurals, and adventure activities.
cards.access_notes: Active student membership and JACard or app entry are required; confirm operating hours and facility availability before visiting.

cards.title: Find the Bronze Duke Dog
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Near Bridgeforth Stadium
cards.notes: Follow public campus paths to the large bronze mascot, take a photo from the plaza, and leave event-controlled areas undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: Close Saturday with one of JMU’s largest mascot landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU documents the 2,100-pound bronze Duke Dog statue outside the Plecker Athletic Performance Center behind Bridgeforth Stadium’s south end zone.
cards.source_title: JMU Centennial Celebration - Duke Dog Statue
cards.access_notes: Outdoor viewing may be affected by athletic-event security, ticketing perimeters, or temporary venue restrictions.

cards.title: Read the Spirit Rock
cards.subtitle: Sunday · East Campus
cards.notes: Finish the weekend by viewing the rock’s current message; photograph it as found and respect nearby classes, events, and painters.
cards.short_summary: See how the campus message changes through layers of student expression.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU describes Spirit Rock as an East Campus canvas where campus artists paint event notices or inspirational messages over accumulated layers of paint.
cards.access_notes: View from public campus space; painting may be governed by current university rules, so check those rules before altering the rock.
